summary: @c1-ease/bank postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded VPS
details: The package ships a `postinstall` lifecycle script (`node beacon.cjs`) and a main entry (`index.js`) that both POST installer metadata — `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` install path, `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc` with TLS verification disabled (`rejectUnauthorized: false`). The beacon fires automatically on `npm install` via the lifecycle hook and again on every `require('@c1-ease/bank')` via `index.js`, which calls `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` and then exports a `Proxy` of no-op functions so consuming bundlers continue past the import. The package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' and ships no functional code — its only effect is the beacon. The `@c1-ease` scope combined with a conspicuously high version (99.0.1) and hollow contents is consistent with a dependency-confusion probe targeting an internal package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
